name: Poulet à la moambe
subtitle: Poulet à la moambe (also spelled mouabe) is chicken cooked in a sauce made from palm nuts, or from canned moambe palm sauce.

parts.text: Poulet à la moambe (also spelled mouabe) is chicken cooked in a sauce made from palm nuts, or from canned moambe palm sauce. The chicken is seasoned and fried, then simmered in the reduced palm sauce with onion and garlic; versions of the dish are found all over the Congo River region.
It is often served with cassava leaves (saka-saka) and white rice; a Belgian broadcaster's version also serves it with sliced banana.

blocks.title: La Moambe
blocks.sub: One version of the dish, as given by RTBF; the steps are summarised in our own words. Recipes differ from cook to cook.
blocks.note: From the Belgian public broadcaster RTBF; uses canned palm sauce and canned saka-saka. Rice and pounded peanuts are listed in the ingredients without a separate step.

steps.text: Heat butter and oil in a large pan, cut the chicken into pieces and brown them well.
Season the browned chicken with salt, black pepper and a teaspoon of pili-pili.
Stir in the stock, then the moambe sauce, followed by sliced onions, crushed garlic, thyme and bay leaves.
Simmer until the sauce is thickened and orange, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
Warm the saka-saka in a small pan with two ladles of the moambe sauce and two pinches of pili-pili.
Make a very hot side sauce by mixing a ladle of the sauce with pili-pili.
Serve everything in separate dishes, with sliced banana.
